evidence.source_sentence: SEM micrographs giving a cross-sectional view of the molded part for the foamed COC as well as COC/CB3 and COC/cCF10 are shown in Figure 3.

Figure 3 SEM image showing the cell morphology for (a) COC, (b) COC/CB3, and (c) COC/cCF10 composite in the LT plane. L, horizontal direction and T, vertical direction. Filler particles are not detectable at given resolution.

Figure 4 Close-up examination of fractured surface of COC/CB3 composite, (a) nonfoamed specimen and (b) foamed specimen, by SEM. CB appears as small clusters of spherical particles in the fractured surface of the matrix.
The largest aggregates of CB found were 0.5 lm in both micrographs in comparison with the nominal cell diameter of 60 lm found in COC/CB3.

The majority of cells were in the range of 30-70 lm, which was similar in magnitude to the average fiber length in the composite.

The foam structure produced by injection molding of the unmodified COC demonstrated a broad range of cell sizes, with finer (<50 lm) bubbles located near the skin of the molded part and very large (>500 lm) bubbles along the centerline.
